name: UE
description: The subscriber's device, made up of the mobile equipment and the USIM or ISIM application on the UICC. It runs the radio, NAS, and IMS client stacks, authenticates with keys held on the card, and talks to the radio access node over the air and to core control functions through NAS or SIP.

name: BTS
description: The GSM radio node that serves one or more cells and terminates the Um air interface. It handles radio transmission, channel coding, and ciphering on the air, and is controlled by a BSC over Abis.

name: BSC
description: The GSM access controller that manages radio resources, channel assignment, and handover for a group of BTSs. It connects to the MSC over the A interface for circuit traffic and to the SGSN over Gb (through its packet control unit) for GPRS.

name: NodeB
description: The UMTS radio base station that terminates the Uu air interface and performs physical-layer processing such as spreading, modulation, and power control. It is controlled by an RNC over Iub.

name: RNC
description: The UTRAN controller that owns radio resource management, RRC signalling, and mobility for the NodeBs below it. It connects to the MSC over Iu-CS, to the SGSN over Iu-PS, to other RNCs over Iur, and with direct tunnel it can send user data straight to an SGW over S12.

name: eNodeB
description: The LTE base station that merges radio access and radio control into one node. It runs RRC, schedules the air interface, selects the MME, carries user data to the SGW over S1-U, and coordinates handover with neighbouring eNodeBs over X2.

name: HeNB-GW
description: An optional gateway that aggregates many femtocell (Home eNodeB) S1 connections toward the core. To the MME it looks like a single eNodeB, which keeps the number of S1 associations small.

name: gNB
description: The 5G NR base station within NG-RAN. It terminates the NR air interface, connects to the AMF over N2 for control and to the UPF over N3 for user data, and talks to other gNBs over Xn. It may be split into central and distributed units.

name: Untrusted non-3GPP AN
description: A WLAN or other non-3GPP IP access that the operator does not trust for direct core attachment. A UE on it reaches the EPC by building an IPsec tunnel to an ePDG, and the access may run its own authentication with the 3GPP AAA Server over SWa.

name: TWAN
description: A WLAN that the operator trusts to connect UEs into the EPC without an ePDG. It authenticates users with the 3GPP AAA Server over STa and builds S2a tunnels to the PGW for each PDN connection.

name: MSC
description: The circuit-switched core node that sets up voice calls, handles mobility for CS services, and delivers SMS. It is usually combined with a VLR, links to BSCs over A and RNCs over Iu-CS, and in LTE networks supports CS fallback over SGs and SRVCC over Sv.

name: VLR
description: A database, normally co-located with the MSC, that keeps a temporary copy of subscription data and the location area for each UE in its service area. It fetches that data from the HLR over the D interface and allocates TMSIs.

name: HLR
description: The master subscriber database for circuit- and packet-switched 2G/3G service. It holds the subscription profile and the current VLR and SGSN for each subscriber, and works with the authentication centre (AuC) to supply authentication vectors over MAP.

name: EIR
description: A database of device identities (IMEIs) and their status, such as allowed, blocked, or tracked. The MSC, SGSN, or MME queries it to check a device before granting service.

name: SGSN
description: The packet-switched serving node for GERAN and UTRAN. It handles GPRS mobility, attach, authentication, and PDP context setup, and forwards user traffic to the GGSN over Gn, or to an SGW over S4 when connected to the EPC.

name: GGSN
description: The GPRS gateway toward external packet data networks. It anchors PDP contexts, allocates UE IP addresses, enforces policy and charging, and routes traffic to the Gi interface.

name: SMS-SC
description: The store-and-forward node that accepts, queues, and delivers short messages. It reaches the serving node for a recipient through an SMS-GMSC and receives mobile-originated messages through an SMS-IWMSC.

name: SMS-GMSC
description: The function that takes a mobile-terminated short message from the SMS-SC, asks the HLR or HSS for routing information, and forwards the message to the serving MSC, SGSN, MME, or SMSF.

name: SMS-IWMSC
description: The function that receives mobile-originated short messages from the serving network and passes them to the subscriber's SMS-SC.

name: SMS Router
description: An optional home-network node on the MT SMS path. It answers routing queries from the SMS-GMSC in place of the HSS, so the GMSC sends the message to the router, which then forwards it to the real serving MSC, SGSN, or MME. Operators use it for SMS home routing and for SMS in MME.

name: MME
description: The main EPC control node. It terminates NAS from the UE, runs authentication with vectors from the HSS, tracks UEs in idle mode, pages them, and selects the SGW and PGW for EPS bearers. Its main peers are the eNodeB (S1-MME), HSS (S6a), SGW (S11), and other MMEs (S10).

name: SGW
description: The user-plane anchor for mobility between eNodeBs and between LTE and 2G/3G. It terminates S1-U tunnels, buffers downlink data for idle UEs and triggers paging through the MME, and relays traffic to the PGW over S5 or S8.

name: PGW
description: The EPC gateway toward external packet data networks. It allocates UE IP addresses, hosts the PCEF for policy and charging enforcement, and terminates S5/S8, S2a, and S2b tunnels so that 3GPP and non-3GPP access share one anchor.

name: HSS
description: The subscriber database for EPS and IMS. It stores subscription profiles, the identity of the serving MME or S-CSCF, and authentication data, and it generates authentication vectors. Its main peers are the MME and SGSN (S6a/S6d), the CSCFs (Cx), application servers (Sh), and the 3GPP AAA Server (SWx).

name: PCRF
description: The EPC policy decision point. It builds PCC rules from subscription data, operator policy, and session information from application functions, and pushes them to the PCEF, BBERF, or TDF. Its main peers are the PCEF (Gx), the AF (Rx), and the OCS (Sy).

name: PCEF
description: The enforcement point for PCC rules, located in the PGW or GGSN. It detects service data flows, applies gating and QoS, and reports usage to online and offline charging systems over Gy and Gz.

name: BBERF
fullName: Bearer Binding and Event Reporting Function
description: A function in an access gateway, such as an SGW using PMIP or a trusted non-3GPP gateway, that binds service flows to bearers and reports access events when the PCEF cannot do so itself. It receives QoS rules from the PCRF over Gxa or Gxc.

name: TDF
description: A function that inspects user traffic to detect applications and reports them to the PCRF over Sd. It can also enforce gating, redirection, or bandwidth limits for the detected applications.

name: TSSF
description: A function on the SGi side that steers detected traffic through operator service chains, such as caches or firewalls. It receives traffic steering control information from the PCRF over St.

name: RCAF
description: A function that gathers RAN user-plane congestion information and identifies the UEs in congested cells. It reports congestion to the PCRF over Np and can share it with the SCEF over Ns.

name: OCS
description: The real-time charging system that rates usage, reserves and deducts credit, and grants quota before service is delivered. It serves the PCEF over Gy, IMS nodes over Ro, and reports spending limit status to the PCRF over Sy.

name: OFCS
description: The post-paid charging chain that collects accounting events from network elements and produces charging data records for billing. Gateways report to it over Gz and IMS nodes over Rf.

name: ePDG
description: The gateway that lets UEs on untrusted non-3GPP access, such as public Wi-Fi, reach the EPC. It terminates IKEv2/IPsec tunnels from the UE over SWu, authenticates the UE through the 3GPP AAA Server over SWm, and builds S2b tunnels to the PGW.

name: 3GPP AAA Server
description: The home-network server that authenticates and authorizes UEs on non-3GPP access using EAP-AKA or EAP-AKA'. It fetches vectors and profiles from the HSS over SWx and serves the ePDG (SWm), TWAN (STa), and PGW (S6b).

name: 3GPP AAA Proxy
description: A visited-network proxy that relays AAA signalling between local non-3GPP access nodes and the home 3GPP AAA Server over SWd. It can apply visited-network policy to roaming users.

name: DRA
description: A Diameter agent that binds all Gx, Rx, and related sessions of one UE IP-CAN session to the same PCRF when several PCRFs serve a network. It works as a proxy or redirect agent.

name: DEA
description: A Diameter relay or proxy at the border of a network that handles all Diameter traffic exchanged with roaming partners. It hides internal topology and gives a single point for inter-network routing and screening.

name: GMLC
description: The entry point for external clients that request a UE's location. It checks privacy, finds the serving node from the HLR, HSS, or UDM, and asks the MSC, SGSN, MME, or AMF to run positioning.

name: E-SMLC
description: The LTE positioning server. On request from the MME over SLs, it selects a positioning method, exchanges LPP messages with the UE and LPPa messages with the eNodeB, and computes the location estimate.

name: SCEF
description: The EPC function that exposes network capabilities to third-party servers through APIs. It supports non-IP data delivery, monitoring events, and parameter provisioning, and talks to the HSS (S6t), the MME and SGSN (T6a/T6b), and the PCRF (Nt).

name: MTC-IWF
description: The function that lets a Services Capability Server send device triggers and other MTC requests into the network over Tsp. It authorizes requests, resolves the device's identity and serving node through the HSS over S6m, and delivers triggers by SMS over T4.

name: MTC-AAA
description: An AAA function for machine-type devices that authenticate over non-3GPP access. It sits with the 3GPP AAA Server or proxy and asks the HSS over S6n for the external identifiers that belong to a device's IMSI.

name: SCS
description: A server, inside or outside the operator domain, that hosts machine-type application logic and reaches devices through the MTC-IWF or SCEF. It requests device triggers and non-IP data delivery.

name: BM-SC
description: The MBMS function that authorizes content providers, schedules broadcast sessions, and starts and stops MBMS bearers. It feeds content to the MBMS-GW (or GGSN in 3G) and signals sessions over SGmb or Gmb.

name: MBMS-GW
description: The gateway that sends MBMS broadcast traffic from the BM-SC to eNodeBs using IP multicast. It signals session start and stop to the MME over Sm.

name: CBC
description: The node that manages public warning and cell broadcast messages. It sends warning content to the radio network through the BSC, RNC, MME (SBc), or AMF (N50) for broadcast in the target area.

name: CSS
description: A visited-network database that holds closed subscriber group information for roaming users. It supplements the home HSS data so that the MME or SGSN can control access to home cells.

name: P-CSCF
description: The first SIP contact point for the UE in IMS. It keeps the security association with the UE, compresses and checks SIP, and acts as the AF toward the PCRF or PCF to set up media bearers. It forwards requests to the I-CSCF or S-CSCF.

name: I-CSCF
description: The SIP entry point into a home IMS network. It queries the HSS to assign or locate the serving S-CSCF during registration and routes incoming requests to it.

name: S-CSCF
description: The IMS registrar and session controller for a user. It authenticates the user with vectors from the HSS, downloads the user profile over Cx, applies initial filter criteria to invoke application servers over ISC, and routes sessions.

name: E-CSCF
description: The CSCF that handles IMS emergency sessions. It receives emergency requests from the P-CSCF, obtains location and routing information, and routes the call to the right emergency centre.

name: BGCF
description: The IMS function that decides where to break out a session toward the circuit-switched network. It picks a local MGCF or forwards the request to a BGCF in another network.

name: MGCF
description: The signalling gateway between IMS and the CS network. It converts SIP to ISUP or BICC and controls an IMS-MGW over Mn to convert the media.

name: IMS-MGW
description: The media gateway that converts RTP media on the IMS side to TDM or other CS bearers, including codec transcoding. It is controlled by an MGCF using H.248.

name: MRFC
description: The controller for IMS media resources such as announcements, conferencing, and transcoding. It receives SIP from the S-CSCF or application servers and controls an MRFP over Mp.

name: MRFP
description: The media processing part of the MRF. It mixes, plays, records, and transcodes media streams under control of the MRFC.

name: IBCF
description: The SIP border function between IMS networks. It applies interconnect policy, hides topology, and can control a transition gateway for media at the network edge.

name: AS
description: A SIP application server that hosts IMS services such as telephony supplementary services, messaging, or voice call continuity. The S-CSCF invokes it over ISC, and it can read and write user data in the HSS over Sh.

name: SLF
description: A lookup function that tells the CSCFs or application servers which HSS holds a user's data when the network has more than one HSS. It answers over Dx and Dh.

name: IP-SM-GW
description: An application server that carries SMS over IMS. It converts between SIP-based messages and the legacy SMS transport, and acts toward the SMS-GMSC like a serving MSC.

name: AF
description: An application-layer function that needs policy control for its sessions, such as the P-CSCF for IMS voice. It gives session and media information to the PCRF over Rx, or to the PCF or NEF in 5GC.

name: BSF (GBA)
description: The GBA function that runs AKA with the UE to create a shared key and bootstrapping transaction identifier. Application servers (NAFs) later fetch derived keys from it to authenticate the UE.

name: NAF
description: An application server that relies on GBA for UE authentication. It obtains application-specific keys from the BSF over Zn, for example to secure XCAP over Ut.

name: AMF
description: The 5GC control node that terminates N1 NAS and N2 toward the access network. It handles registration, connection and reachability management, mobility, and access authentication with the AUSF, and relays session management messages to the SMF.

name: SMF
description: The 5GC function that sets up, modifies, and releases PDU sessions. It allocates UE IP addresses, selects and controls UPFs over N4, applies policy from the PCF, and reports charging to the CHF.

name: UPF
description: The 5GC user-plane node. It forwards and routes packets, acts as the anchor for mobility and the connection point to the data network, applies QoS and usage reporting, and follows rules installed by the SMF over N4.

name: PCF
description: The 5GC policy decision point. It provides session, access and mobility, and UE policies to the SMF, AMF, and UE, and reads policy subscription data from the UDR.

name: NEF
description: The 5GC function that exposes network capabilities and events to external application functions in a controlled way. It translates between external and internal identifiers and can store exposed data in the UDR.

name: NRF
description: The service registry of the 5GC. NFs register their profiles with it, and other NFs query it to discover peers and obtain access tokens for service-based calls.

name: UDM
description: The 5GC front end for subscriber data. It generates authentication credentials, holds the registration of the serving AMF and SMF, and provides subscription data to other NFs, storing it in the UDR.

name: AUSF
description: The home-network function that runs 5G AKA or EAP-AKA' for the UE on request from the AMF. It gets vectors from the UDM and confirms the authentication result to the serving network.

name: N3IWF
description: The 5GC gateway for UEs on untrusted non-3GPP access. It terminates the UE's IPsec tunnels over NWu, relays NAS to the AMF over N2, and carries user data to the UPF over N3.

name: UDR
description: The 5GC database that stores subscription, policy, application, and exposure data. The UDM, PCF, and NEF read and write it through the Nudr service.

name: UDSF
description: An optional 5GC store that any NF can use to keep its unstructured context data, such as UE or session context, outside the NF instance so that other instances can pick it up.

name: SMSF
description: The 5GC function that delivers SMS over NAS. It registers with the UDM, checks SMS subscription, and relays messages between the AMF and the SMS-GMSC or SMS-IWMSC.

name: NSSF
description: The 5GC function that selects the network slice instances to serve a UE. It works out the allowed NSSAI and the AMF set or NRF to use during registration.

name: 5G-EIR
description: The 5GC equipment identity check function. The AMF asks it whether a device's PEI is allowed or blocked.

name: LMF
description: The 5G positioning server. It selects positioning methods, exchanges positioning protocol messages with the UE and NG-RAN through the AMF, and computes the UE location.

name: SEPP
description: The border proxy for service-based signalling between PLMNs. It protects and filters inter-PLMN messages, hides topology, and exchanges N32 traffic with the SEPP of the partner network.

name: NWDAF
description: The 5GC analytics function. It collects data from NFs and OAM, produces statistics and predictions such as load or UE mobility, and provides them to NFs and AFs on request or subscription.

name: CHF
description: The 5G converged charging function. It provides online and offline charging over the Nchf service and supplies spending limit status to the PCF.

name: SCP
description: An optional proxy for service-based signalling inside a PLMN. It routes requests, can perform discovery and selection on behalf of consumers, and gives a point for load balancing.

name: BSF
description: The 5GC function that stores which PCF serves a given PDU session, keyed by UE address, DNN, and slice. AFs and other NFs query it to find the right PCF.

name: UCMF
description: The function that stores UE radio capability sets and maps them to short UE radio capability IDs, so that the network can avoid sending full capability information.

name: NSSAAF
fullName: Network Slice-Specific Authentication and Authorization Function
description: The function that runs slice-specific authentication between the UE and an external AAA server, relaying EAP between the AMF and the AAA server.

name: NSACF
description: The function that counts registered UEs and PDU sessions per network slice and checks them against configured quotas. The AMF and SMF ask it before admitting a UE or session.

name: TNGF
description: The 5GC gateway for UEs on trusted non-3GPP access. It terminates N2 and N3 toward the core and the IPsec connections from the UE over NWt.

name: TWIF
description: The function that connects devices on trusted WLAN that cannot run 5GC NAS. It acts on the device's behalf toward the AMF over N2 and the UPF over N3.

name: W-AGF
description: The function that connects wireline access networks, such as cable or fixed broadband, to the 5GC. It terminates N2 and N3 on behalf of the wireline residential gateway.

name: DN
description: The external or operator packet network a UE reaches through the core, such as the internet or an IMS network. It is reached from the GGSN over Gi, the PGW over SGi, and the UPF over N6.

name: CS-MGW
description: The media gateway of a split CS core. It terminates CS bearers from the access and the PSTN and handles codec conversion, echo cancelling, and bearer control under an MSC Server or GMSC Server over Mc.

name: GMSC
description: The MSC that receives calls entering the PLMN for a mobile subscriber. It interrogates the HLR for routing information and routes the call to the MSC serving the subscriber; in a split core it is a GMSC Server plus a CS-MGW.

name: HNB
description: A customer-premises UMTS small cell. It provides UTRAN coverage in homes or offices and reaches the core through an HNB-GW over Iuh, usually across a broadband connection; closed access is controlled with CSG lists.

name: HNB-GW
description: The gateway that aggregates Home NodeBs toward the core. It terminates Iuh and makes the HNBs it serves appear as a single RNS on Iu-CS to the MSC and Iu-PS to the SGSN.

name: ANDSF
fullName: Access Network Discovery and Selection Function
description: An optional server that gives UEs network discovery and selection data for non-3GPP accesses. It provides access network discovery information and inter-system mobility and routing policies over S14, by push or on request.

name: CSG List Server
description: A server that provisions the Allowed CSG list and Operator CSG list on the UE. It updates the lists by OMA DM or by OTA updates to the USIM, and the lists apply to both HNB and HeNB cells.

name: AuC
description: The function associated with an HLR that stores each subscriber's secret key. It generates the authentication, integrity, and ciphering data the HLR passes to the VLR, SGSN, and MME, and is usually part of the HLR or HSS.

name: GCR
description: A register that holds the attributes of voice group call (VGCS) and voice broadcast (VBS) calls. The MSC queries it for the cells and MSCs a group call covers and for which MSC is responsible for the call.

name: SMLC
description: The GERAN positioning server, either part of the BSC or a separate node reached over Lb. It schedules positioning resources, may control LMUs, and calculates the final location estimate and its accuracy.

name: SAS
description: A standalone UTRAN positioning server connected to the RNC over Iupc. It provides positioning assistance data, such as GPS assistance, and calculates location estimates when the RNC does not compute them itself.

name: LCS Client
description: An application outside the PLMN that requests the location of a target UE. It sends requests to the GMLC over Le and receives location estimates, subject to the subscriber's privacy settings.

name: gsmSCF
description: The CAMEL service control point that runs operator-specific service logic, such as prepaid. It controls calls through the gsmSSF and GPRS sessions through the gprsSSF and interfaces with the HLR and the gsmSRF.

name: gprsSSF
description: The CAMEL switching function in the SGSN, derived from the IN service switching function. It detects triggers in GPRS sessions and PDP contexts and asks the gsmSCF for instructions over Ge, for example for prepaid data.

name: IM-SSF
description: An IMS application server that hosts CAMEL services for IMS sessions. It interworks SIP on ISC with CAP toward the gsmSCF and fetches CAMEL subscription data from the HSS over Si.

name: TrGW
description: A media gateway at an IMS network border, controlled by the IBCF over Ix. It provides network address and port translation and IPv4/IPv6 translation for session media, and forwards media to peer networks over Izi.

name: IMS-AGW
description: A media gateway on the access side of the P-CSCF, controlled over Iq. It allocates media transport addresses, applies NAT traversal, policing, and marking to media flows, and can terminate media security.

name: WLAN AN
description: The WLAN access network in I-WLAN interworking, made up of access points and AAA proxies. It authenticates users through the 3GPP AAA Server over Wa and routes their traffic to the WAG over Wn.

name: WAG
description: The I-WLAN gateway between the WLAN and the 3GPP network, in the visited network when roaming. It filters, polices, and collects charging data for the traffic between the WLAN UE and the PDG.

name: PDG
description: The I-WLAN gateway that gives WLAN UEs access to 3GPP PS services. It terminates the UE's Wu tunnel and connects to packet data networks over Wi, in the home or visited network; the ePDG evolved from it.

name: MCE
description: The E-UTRAN function that coordinates MBMS across the eNodeBs of an MBSFN area. It handles admission control and radio resource allocation for broadcast and relays session control from the MME over M3 to eNodeBs over M2.

name: GUP Server
description: A single point of access to a subscriber's Generic User Profile data. It serves application requests over Rg and locates the repositories, such as the HSS, that hold each profile component.

name: SPR
description: The repository of subscriber and subscription data that the PCRF uses for policy and charging decisions. The PCRF reads it over Sp, and the UDR can take its place in a converged data architecture.

name: BPCF
description: The policy function of a fixed broadband access network. In fixed-mobile interworking it receives QoS policy from the PCRF over S9a and applies it to the broadband access, so traffic from HNBs, HeNBs, and WLANs gets the right treatment.

name: PFDF
description: A repository of Packet Flow Descriptions that third-party SCS/ASs manage through the SCEF over Nu. It provides the PFDs to the PCEF over Gw and the TDF over Gwn for application detection.

name: GCS AS
description: The application server for group communication over LTE. It sends media and signalling to groups of UEs over unicast EPS bearers, MBMS broadcast through the BM-SC over MB2, or both.

name: ProSe Function
description: The network function for proximity services, with one logical instance per PLMN. It authorises and provisions UEs for direct discovery and communication, allocates ProSe Application Codes, and supports EPC-level discovery.

name: ProSe AS
description: The application server behind a ProSe application. It stores application user identities and their mapping to EPC identities, and works with the ProSe Function over PC2 for EPC-level discovery and name translation.

name: SLP
description: The OMA SUPL server for user-plane positioning. It locates UEs over an IP connection with assistance data and measurements, and answers location queries, such as those from the ProSe Function over PC4b.

name: HRPD AN
description: The 3GPP2 CDMA2000 high-rate packet data radio network. It interworks with E-UTRAN through the MME over S101 and S121 for pre-registration, optimised handover, and RAN information exchange with neighbouring eNodeBs.

name: 1xCS IWS
description: The 3GPP2 interworking function toward CDMA2000 1xRTT circuit-switched networks. It exchanges tunnelled 1x CS signalling with the MME over S102 to support SRVCC and CS fallback from E-UTRAN to 1x voice.

name: HSGW
description: The 3GPP2 HRPD gateway that connects eHRPD access to the EPC PDN GW over S2a. During E-UTRAN to HRPD handover it receives forwarded downlink data from the Serving GW over S103.

name: AFE
description: A function in the User Data Convergence architecture that keeps its application logic but stores no user data locally, such as an HLR, HSS, AS, or PCRF front end. It reads and updates user data in the UDR over Ud.

name: Content Provider
description: A third-party or operator service that supplies content for MBMS delivery. It creates and controls MBMS user services and sends content to the BM-SC over xMB, either directly or through the SCEF.

name: I-SMF
description: An SMF inserted into a PDU session when the UE is outside the anchor SMF's service area. It talks to the AMF over N11 and to the anchor SMF over N16a, and controls the UPFs the anchor SMF cannot reach. The anchor SMF keeps the PCF and CHF interfaces.

name: TSCTSF
fullName: Time Sensitive Communication and Time Synchronization Function
description: The function that handles AF requests for time synchronization and time sensitive QoS. It checks them against subscription data, builds TSC assistance containers for the PCF, and controls (g)PTP and access stratum time distribution.

name: EASDF
description: A DNS handling function for edge computing. The SMF provides it as the UE's DNS server and gives it rules for each PDU session, so it can steer DNS queries toward suitable local edge application servers and report DNS events.

name: NSWOF
description: The function that lets a UE use its 5GS credentials on a WLAN for non-seamless offload. It acts as a 3GPP AAA server toward the WLAN over SWa and translates to the AUSF over N60.

name: DCCF
description: The function that coordinates data and analytics collection for consumers such as the NWDAF. It picks the data sources, avoids duplicate collection, and delivers data itself or through a messaging framework via the MFAF.

name: MFAF
description: The adaptor between 5GC data sources and an operator messaging framework outside 3GPP scope. Under DCCF control it receives data from sources, then processes, formats, and sends it to consumers or notification endpoints.

name: ADRF
description: The repository for collected data, analytics, and ML models. NWDAFs and the DCCF store and retrieve data and analytics in it, and NWDAFs with model training store trained ML model files there.

name: MB-SMF
description: The session management function for 5G multicast and broadcast services. It allocates TMGIs, creates and updates MBS sessions, and controls the MB-UPF over N4mb so it delivers the multicast and broadcast traffic.

name: MBSF
description: The service-layer function for 5G multicast and broadcast services. It handles MBS session requests from the AF or NEF, interacts with the MB-SMF, and controls the MBSTF that handles the MBS payload.

name: 5G DDNMF
description: The 5GC function for ProSe direct discovery. It allocates and checks the discovery codes UEs use to find each other over the PC5 sidelink, using ProSe authorization data from the UDM.

name: PWS-IWF
description: The function that lets a CBC without 5GC support deliver public warning messages over 5G. It talks to the CBC over SBc and to the AMF over the service-based interface.

name: SGW-C
description: The control part of a split SGW. It terminates S11 and the control plane of S5/S8, selects the SGW-U, and controls it over Sxa. Together with the SGW-U it provides the full SGW functionality.

name: SGW-U
description: The user-plane part of a split SGW. Under SGW-C control over Sxa, it terminates S1-U and S5/S8 user- plane tunnels, forwards packets, buffers downlink data for idle UEs, and reports usage.

name: PGW-C
description: The control part of a split PGW. It allocates UE IP addresses, terminates Gx and Gy toward the PCRF and OCS, and controls the PGW-U over Sxb. For 5GS interworking it is combined with the SMF as PGW-C+SMF.

name: PGW-U
description: The user-plane part of a split PGW. Under PGW-C control over Sxb, it terminates S5/S8 user-plane tunnels and SGi, detects service data flows, enforces QoS and gating, and reports usage.

name: TDF-C
fullName: Traffic Detection Function Control plane function
description: The control part of a split TDF. It terminates Sd toward the PCRF and Gyn or Gzn for charging, selects the TDF-U, and installs application detection, enforcement, and usage reporting rules in it over Sxc.

name: TDF-U
fullName: Traffic Detection Function User plane function
description: The user-plane part of a split TDF. Under TDF-C control over Sxc, it inspects traffic to detect applications, enforces gating, redirection, and bandwidth limits, and reports usage to the TDF-C.

name: SGW/PGW-C
description: The control part of a combined SGW and PGW with split control and user planes. It provides SGW-C and PGW-C functions in one node and controls the combined user-plane function over Sxa/Sxb.

name: SGW/PGW-U
description: The user-plane part of a combined SGW and PGW with split control and user planes. It provides SGW-U and PGW-U functions in one node under control of the combined SGW/PGW-C over Sxa/Sxb.

name: gNB-CU-CP
description: The control-plane part of a gNB central unit. It hosts RRC and the control-plane PDCP, terminates N2 toward the AMF and Xn-C toward peer nodes, and controls gNB-DUs over F1-C and gNB-CU-UPs over E1.

name: gNB-CU-UP
description: The user-plane part of a gNB central unit. It hosts SDAP and user-plane PDCP, terminates N3 toward the UPF, and exchanges user data with gNB-DUs over F1-U under gNB-CU-CP control over E1.

name: gNB-DU
description: The distributed unit of a split gNB. It hosts the RLC, MAC, and physical layers serving one or more cells, and connects to the gNB-CU over F1. Its operation is partly controlled by the gNB-CU.

name: CDF
description: The offline charging function that receives charging events from network elements, for example over Rf, and builds CDRs from them in near real time. It sends the CDRs to the CGF over Ga.

name: CGF
description: The offline charging function that receives CDRs from the CDF over Ga. It validates, consolidates, and stores them in CDR files, and transfers the files to the billing domain over Bx.
